---
title: "Within a single model"
subtitle: "Example 7: comparing the effects of different variables"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

`mecompare` can be used to calculate marginal effects within a single model, 
and compare those effects using [`metest`](../../metest/index.html). 
Here: does a college degree or being married have the larger association 
with being very happy?

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/gss_cme", clear
drop if year < 2000
drop if employed != 1
drop if missing(vhappy, college, wages, occprest, age, married, parent, woman, conserv, reltrad)

quietly logit vhappy i.college i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.race i.reltrad ///
              i.year c.age##c.age c.occprest, vce(robust)
estimates store happymod
<</dd_do>>
```

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare i.college i.married, models(happymod)
<</dd_do>>
```

`metest` takes an expression referring to the row numbers from the `#` column 
in the `mecompare` output. The difference between the two marginal effects, 
with its standard error:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 2 - 1
<</dd_do>>
```

Any linear or nonlinear combination of rows works the same way -- for example a
ratio, `metest 2 / 1`, or a test that several effects are equal,
`metest 1 = 2`.
